findings.failure_path: For a production multi-component failure, the mandatory boundary walk tells the agent to log entry/exit data and received env/config at every boundary. Those values can contain credentials, customer payloads, or proprietary configuration and are emitted into shared telemetry before Phase B's later copy-time sanitization can apply or retract them.
findings.smallest_fix: At this firing step, require allowlisted/redacted metadata rather than raw payloads or config; explicitly forbid logging secrets, credentials, headers, bodies, PII, and raw env/config, and route unsafe cases to existing access-controlled telemetry or synthetic probes.

findings.failure_path: The Sources section contains normative attribution summaries, but the bounded packet supplies only the candidate's own paraphrases and self-review assertions—not primary-page excerpts or other independently checkable source evidence. Claims such as the survey findings and debug-gym conclusions therefore cannot be verified under the required diff-only review, allowing a mistaken attribution to pass while violating an explicit acceptance condition.
findings.smallest_fix: Add bounded, reviewable primary-source evidence for each changed attribution—page/section locator plus the supporting short excerpt—or remove the unsupported attributed claim from the landed text.

challenge_focus: Gate-fireability and bypass-by-omission of the new diagnosis rules (probe ordering, in-loop hypothesis log, causality-plus-incorrectness fix gate, boundary walk, suite bisection, upstream trace, observe-not-infer, telemetry substitute for irreproducible symptoms, pathspec bisect narrowing); data-leak or data-loss paths in instrumentation and evidence handling; contradictions with the existing falsify-first, three-strike, complexity-verdict, and sanitization rules; over-broad absolutes that would cost rounds on simple deterministic bugs; accuracy of the playbook Sources section against the primary pages.
